Active from 1929 to 1941, this organized crime enforcement squad carried out between 400 and 1,000 contract killings for the National Crime Syndicate before being exposed by a turncoat member nicknamed 'Kid Twist.' What was this group called?
Murder, Inc.: American organized crime groups in the 1930s and 1940s.
Nicknamed 'Bat'ko' (Father), this Ukrainian revolutionary commanded an Insurgent Army and tried to build anarchist communism among the peasantry around Huliaipole between 1918 and 1921 — who was he?
The younger sister of Japan's first great unifier, this Sengoku-period noblewoman was mother to three daughters who each became prominent in their own right — who was she?
Oichi: Historical figure in the late Sengoku period (1547–1583)

Known to the Rus as the Obri and to the Göktürks as the Apar, this nomadic confederation ruled a khaganate centered on the Carpathian Basin from the late sixth to early ninth centuries — who were they?
Pannonian Avars: Alliance of various Eurasian nomads – 6th to 9th centuries.
Unlike business, which serves private gain, this practice channels private initiative toward the public good and quality of life — what is it called?
Philanthropy: Private efforts to increase public good.
This French politician served as government spokesperson for the Attal administration in 2024 after being elected deputy for Hauts-de-Seine's 8th constituency — who is she?
This self-described separatist was at the center of a 1992 armed standoff with federal agents in Idaho that left his wife and son dead, and he later received $3.1 million in compensation — who is he?

A top West Point graduate and U.S. Army engineer for 32 years, he switched sides to command the Army of Northern Virginia until its 1865 surrender, earning fame as one of the war's craftiest tacticians. Which Confederate general is it?
Robert E. Lee: Confederate States Army general (1807–1870)
Serving as Grand Vizier under Süleyman the Magnificent, this Ottoman statesman married the sultan's daughter Mihrimah in 1539, earning an epithet meaning 'son-in-law' — who is he?
Rüstem Pasha: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire (1544–1553, 1555–1561)

Taking his regnal name — which meant "the legitimate king" — from an ancient ruler of Akkad, this Neo-Assyrian monarch founded a new dynastic line and aspired to conquer the known world before dying in battle in 705 BC. Who was he?
Sargon II: King of the Neo-Assyrian Empire. Over the course of his seventeen-year reign, Sargon substantially expanded Assyrian territory and enacted important political and military reforms.
Born in 1940, she is the eldest child of the last Shah of Iran and his first wife, Fawzia of Egypt — who is she?

It began as a Cold War quarrel over how to read Marx — Mao branding Moscow's de-Stalinization and 'peaceful coexistence' as revisionism — and slowly froze relations between two communist giants. What is this rift called?
Names of the days of the week
Racial segregation in the United States
Sino-Soviet split: Conflict between communist blocs.
A former professor turned politician, this leader has served in India's upper house of parliament since 2019 and acts as a senior national spokesperson for the Bharatiya Janata Party — who is he?
Prince Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn
Younger brother of a U.S. president and an attorney general, he represented Massachusetts in the Senate from 1962 until his death in 2009 — which long-serving senator?
Ted Kennedy: American lawyer and politician (1932–2009)

Beginning with the death of Russia's last Rurik ruler in 1598 and ending with the Romanov dynasty's rise in 1613, this era of famine, false pretenders, and foreign occupation devastated Russia — what is it called?
Time of Troubles: 1598–1613 chaotic period of Russian history.
In 2023, 1.3 million applicants competed for just 1,255 government job openings through this Indian constitutional body's exams — what is it?
Union Public Service Commission: India's central recruiting agency.

Ruling for just eight months during the chaotic Year of the Four Emperors, this Roman ruler took the honorific Germanicus instead of Caesar and tried to boost his popularity by imitating the still-beloved Nero — who was he?
Carved out of the Carolingian Empire at the Treaty of Verdun in 843 and lasting until the Capetians took over in 987, which kingdom was the very first stage of what we now call France?
West Francia: Predecessor of France from 843 to 987.
The paramount leader of China since 2012, this politician served as general secretary of the Communist Party and was sent to a rural village as a teenager during the Cultural Revolution. Who is he?
Xi Jinping: Leader of China since 2012. Xi Jinping (born 15 June 1953) is a Chinese politician who is the paramount leader of China.
This Chinese politician led the Communist Party's anti-corruption watchdog from 2017 to 2022 before becoming chairman of the National People's Congress Standing Committee — who is he?
Which of these people was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four. Richards graduated from Westford Academy (second oldest secondary school in Massachusetts) in 1862.
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Henrietta Swan Leavitt is an astronomer. Henrietta Swan Leavitt (July 4, 1868 – December 12, 1921) was an American astronomer.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Augustus De Morgan is a mathematician. Augustus De Morgan (27 June 1806 – 18 March 1871) was a British mathematician and logician.
What is the atomic number of Technetium?
Technetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
What is the atomic number of Sulfur?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
In what year was Paul Allen born?
Paul Allen: Paul Gardner Allen (January 21, 1953 – October 15, 2018) was an American businessman, computer programmer, and investor.
In what year was Arthur Schopenhauer born?
Arthur Schopenhauer (22 February 1788 – 21 September 1860) was a German philosopher and writer.
In what year was Lex Fridman born?
Lex Fridman: Alexei "Lex" Fridman (born 15 August 1983) is an American computer scientist and podcaster.
In what year did Mario Molina die?
Mario Molina: Mario José Molina-Pasquel Henríquez (19 March 1943 – 7 October 2020) was a Mexican physical chemist.
In what year did Edward Teller die?
Edward Teller: Born in Austria-Hungary in 1908, Teller emigrated to the US in the 1930s, one of the many so-called "Martians", a group of Hungarian scientist émigrés.
In what year was Möbius strip discovered?
Möbius strip: In mathematics, a Möbius strip, Möbius band, or Möbius loop is a surface that can be formed by attaching the ends of a strip of paper together with a half-twist.
R (programming language): Robert Gentleman. R is a programming language for statistical computing and data visualization.
Prunus domestica: People's Republic of China. Prunus domestica is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.
In which country is IAI Kfir?
Who is credited with discovering Eta Carinae?
Eta Carinae: Pieter Dirkszoon Keyser. It became the second-brightest star in the night sky between 11–14 March 1843 before fading well below naked-eye visibility after 1856.
Who is credited with discovering Benzene?
Benzene: Michael Faraday. Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6.
Who is credited with discovering Vanadium?
Vanadium: Andrés Manuel del Río. Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.

This British Formula One engineer, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest designers, has served as technical chief at Williams, McLaren, and Red Bull, and now co-owns Aston Martin's F1 team — who is he?
Adrian Newey (born 26 December 1958) is a British engineer, aerodynamicist, automotive designer, and motorsport executive.

Caused by brain damage, disease, or sometimes sedative drugs, this condition splits into a retrograde type that erases memories before an event and an anterograde type that blocks new ones from forming — what is it called?
Amnesia is a deficit in memory caused by brain damage or brain diseases, but it can also be temporarily caused by the use of various sedative and hypnotic drugs.
Linked to smoking, high blood pressure and older age, this silent widening of the body's main artery to over 1.5 times normal size can suddenly rupture with severe abdominal pain — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm is an enlargement (dilatation) of the aorta to greater than 1.5 times normal size.
This American psychologist developed the philosophy of radical behaviorism and pioneered operant conditioning while a longtime professor at Harvard — who is he?
B. F. Skinner (March 20, 1904 - August 18, 1990) was an American psychologist, behaviorist, inventor, and social philosopher.

The bassist of a legendary British rock band from 1962 to 1993, performing on its first 19 studio albums, this musician was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989 as part of that group — who is he?
Bill Wyman (n Perks; born 24 October 1936) is an English musician who was the bassist of the rock band the Rolling Stones from 1962 to 1993.
One of the largest, longest-lived trees in the Amazon, this species produces a fruit and shell weighing up to two kilograms, with edible seeds famed for their selenium content — what tree is it?
Brazil nut (Bertholletia excelsa) refers to a South American tree of the monotypic genus Bertholletia in the family Lecythidaceae as well as the tree's commercially-harvested edible seeds.

Spread through contact with infected feces and capable of killing up to 91% of untreated cases, this highly contagious virus mainly strikes dogs and wolves but can also infect foxes, cats, and skunks — what's the virus?
Canine parvovirus (also referred to as CPV, CPV2, or parvo) is a contagious virus mainly affecting dogs and wolves.
This English polymath is credited with inventing the first mechanical computer and designing an unrealized 'analytical engine' programmed using ideas borrowed from the Jacquard loom. Who is he?
Charles Babbage (26 December 1791 - 18 October 1871) was an English polymath.
Born near Toulouse, this French inventor is remembered chiefly as an aviation pioneer — though in 1870 he was also an early enthusiast of cycling in France; who was he?
Clément Ader (French; 2 April 1841 - 3 May 1925) was a French inventor and engineer who was born near Toulouse in Muret, Haute-Garonne, and died in Toulouse.
Derived from Greek words meaning universe and study of, this scientific and philosophical field examines the nature of existence at the grandest scale — what is it called?
Cosmology (from Ancient Greek (cosmos) 'the universe, the world' and - (logia) 'study of') is the study of the nature of the universe, the cosmos.
Specialists in this branch of medicine handle skin infections, cancers, hair loss, and cosmetic concerns, sometimes even life-threatening conditions like severe burns — which medical field?
Dermatology is the branch of medicine dealing with the skin.
Sometimes triggered by lead poisoning or reactions to neuroleptic drugs, this neurological disorder produces involuntary, twisting muscle contractions — what is it?

Dystonia is a neurological hyperkinetic movement disorder in which sustained or repetitive muscle contractions occur involuntarily, resulting in twisting and repetitive movements or abnormal fixed postures.

Native only to a single island in French Polynesia, this arum-family plant is now one of the world's most popular houseplants, and an ecologically damaging invasive species from South Africa to the Pacific Islands. Name it?
Epipremnum aureum is a species in the arum family Araceae, native to Mo'orea in the Society Islands of French Polynesia.

Named for a physicist who reportedly asked 'But where is everybody?' over lunch in 1950, this puzzle contrasts the vast odds of alien civilizations with our total lack of evidence for them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox is the term for the apparent gap between the lack of conclusive evidence of extraterrestrial civilizations and the apparently high likelihood of their existence.
Son of a wealthy Greek architect, this 2nd-century physician and philosopher's writings shaped anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, and neurology for centuries after his death — who is he?
As emeritus chairman of the company he co-founded, this American engineer lent his name to a law predicting steady doubling of transistor counts on integrated circuits — who is he?
Gordon Moore (January 3, 1929 - March 24, 2023) was an American businessman, scientist, engineer, and the co-founder and emeritus chairman of Intel Corporation.
This usually benign tumor made of blood vessels typically appears on a baby's skin at birth or within weeks, often on the face, scalp, chest, or back, then shrinks over childhood — what is it?
Hemangioma is a usually benign vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Dissolved in water it yields a notoriously corrosive acid, yet it's also the main industrial route to fluorine and a feedstock for Teflon-style polymers like PTFE — which colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen fluoride is an inorganic compound with chemical formula HF.
Founder of Romania's Social Democratic Party, this engineer served two separate stints as president after playing a leading role in the 1989 revolution that toppled Ceaușescu — who is he?

Ion Iliescu (3 March 1930 - 5 August 2025) was a Romanian politician and engineer who served as the first and third President of Romania since the country's transition to democracy, from 1990 to 1996 and 2000 to 2004.
The youngest division chief in GM history, this engineer shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the company behind a famously gull-winged car — who was he?
John DeLorean (d-; January 6, 1925 - March 19, 2005) was an American engineer, inventor, and executive in the U.S.
Despite its name suggesting a root vegetable, this biennial cultivar of wild cabbage grows a swollen edible stem above ground and is related to broccoli, kale, and Brussels sprouts — what is it?
Kohlrabi (scientific name Brassica oleracea Gongylodes Group), also called German turnip or turnip cabbage, is a biennial vegetable, a low, stout cultivar of wild cabbage.
Found in the support tissues of most plants, this polymer resists rot and reinforces wood and bark structure — what is it?
Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.
This genus of Old World monkeys includes 23 species ranging from Asia and North Africa all the way to Gibraltar, and mostly eats fruit — what is it?
Macaque (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.

Designed as both fighter and ground-attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation), this all-weather supersonic, carrier-capable twin-engined jet was derived from the YF-17 and developed for the Navy. What aircraft is this?

McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet is an all-weather supersonic, twin-engined, carrier-capable, multirole combat aircraft, designed as both a fighter and ground attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation).
Also called selective sound sensitivity syndrome, this disorder causes specific everyday sounds to trigger intense, disproportionate emotional and physiological distress — what is it?
Misophonia (or selective sound sensitivity syndrome) is a disorder of decreased tolerance to specific sounds or their associated stimuli, or cues.
Found from Africa to Southeast Asia, this snake genus contains the 'true cobras' as opposed to look-alikes like the king cobra — which genus?
Naja is a genus of venomous elapid snakes commonly known as cobras (or "true cobras").
Built from nucleotide units of a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogenous base, these biomolecules come in two main classes distinguished by whether their sugar is ribose or deoxyribose — what are they?
Nucleic acid are large biomolecules that are crucial in all cells and viruses.
Belonging to the pea family and native to Mesoamerica, this vine produces blue or white flowers and an edible tuberous root known in Spanish as jícama — which species?
Pachyrhizus erosus (from Nahuatl languages: xicamatl) or Mexican turnip, is a native Mesoamerican vine, although the name jicama most commonly refers to the plant's edible tuberous root.
This serous membrane lines the abdominal cavity, wrapping most internal organs in a single sheet of mesothelium that also carries their blood vessels and nerves — what's the membrane?
Peritoneum is the serous membrane forming the lining of the abdominal cavity or coelom in amniotes and some invertebrates, such as annelids.

This common skin condition begins with a single scaly 'herald patch,' followed weeks later by an eruption of smaller pinkish spots, and typically clears on its own within three months. What is it called?
Pityriasis rosea is a type of skin rash.

An Italian chemist and Auschwitz survivor, he wrote a celebrated memoir of his year in the camp and later a book of stories each named for a chemical element, hailed as the best science book ever — who was he?
Primo Levi (31 July 1919 - 11 April 1987) was a Jewish Italian chemist, partisan, Holocaust survivor and writer.
This Indian Air Force pilot became the first Indian ever to travel to space, flying aboard a Soviet Soyuz mission in 1984 — who is he?
Rakesh Sharma (born 13 January 1949) is an Indian cosmonaut and a pilot of the Indian Air Force.
Named for its type genus, this plant family of nearly 4,800 species includes the trees and shrubs behind apples, pears, plums, cherries, and peaches — what family is it?
Rosaceae is a family of flowering plants that includes 4,828 known species in 91 genera.

Native to the North Pacific coasts, this marine mammal is the heaviest member of the weasel family yet one of the smallest marine mammals, insulated by the densest fur coat in the animal kingdom — what is it?
Sea otter (Enhydra lutris) is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.
Despite the name, this digestive organ is about 6.5 metres long; it's just narrower in diameter than its large counterpart. What organ is it?
Small intestine is an organ in the gastrointestinal tract where most of the absorption of nutrients from food takes place.
CEO of Microsoft from 2000 to 2014, this American businessman later became the billionaire owner of the Los Angeles Clippers — who is he?
Steve Ballmer (born March 24, 1956) is an American businessman and investor who was the chief executive officer of Microsoft from 2000 to 2014.
Found naturally in grapes and other fruits, this crystalline compound's potassium salt is better known as cream of tartar, a key ingredient in homemade baking powder — which compound?
Tartaric acid is a white, crystalline organic acid that occurs naturally in many fruits, most notably in grapes but also in tamarinds, bananas, avocados, and citrus.
This family of large, long-legged flies can be identified by a maxillary-palp segment longer than the other three combined, and typically has thirteen segments in each antenna. Name the family?
Tipulidae is a family of large crane flies in the order Diptera.
This bodily fluid, produced by the kidneys to flush out urea and other waste, can also serve a second life as a nitrogen-rich fertilizer for soil — what is it?
Urine is the fluid excreted by the kidneys of vertebrates to clear the bloodstream of excess water and metabolic by-products including urea, uric acid, and creatinine.
Intermediate in size between the Greyhound and the Italian Greyhound, this gentle, minimal-shedding sighthound turns into a bundle of energy the moment it's outdoors — which breed?
Whippet is a British breed of sighthound. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.
Named for its standard passenger capacity, this twin-engine turboprop regional airliner is assembled in Toulouse by a Franco-Italian manufacturer that is half-owned by Airbus — what aircraft is this?
ATR 72: Regional turboprop airliner. The ATR 72 is a twin-engine turboprop, short-haul regional airliner developed and produced in France and Italy by aircraft manufacturer ATR.
Sold as button, cremini, or portobello depending on its stage of maturity, this cultivated mushroom is grown in more than 70 countries — what species is it?
Agaricus bisporus: Species of fungus. Agaricus bisporus, commonly known as the cultivated mushroom, is a basidiomycete mushroom native to grasslands in Eurasia and North America.
Approved for medical use in the US in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowers uric acid to prevent gout and certain kidney stones — what medication is it?
Allopurinol: Medication. Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
Comprising more than 140 species across 16 genera, this small, oily forage fish is found everywhere from the Atlantic to the Black Sea — what is it?
Known by common names like greenfly and blackfly, these small sap-sucking insects reproduce via live-born nymphs without males, a trick called telescoping generations — what are they?
Aphid: Superfamily of insects. The group includes the fluffy white woolly aphids.
This chronic airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath when triggers like pollen or dust make the bronchioles constrict and fill with mucus — what condition is it?
Asthma: Long-term inflammatory disease of the airways of the lungs.
Also called Asian sea bass, this catadromous fish is widely distributed from the Middle East across South and Southeast Asia to Oceania — which fish?
Barramundi: Species of fish. The species is widely distributed in the Indo-West Pacific, spanning the waters of the Middle East, South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania.
Split into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism, this scientific field studies the chemical processes that occur within living organisms — which field?

Biochemistry: Study of chemical processes of living organisms. Biochemistry, or biological chemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.
Developed from a wide-body airliner and selected in 2011 to replace an aging fleet of aerial tankers, this refueling aircraft entered US Air Force service in 2019 — which aircraft?
Boeing KC-46 Pegasus: American military aerial refueling and transport aircraft.
Native to Australia and naturally green and yellow with black scalloped markings, this small, long-tailed parrot is one of the world's most popular pet birds — what is it?
Encompassing wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals, which genus is defined by its members' massive skulls, long legs, and comparatively short ears and tails?
Canis: Genus of canines. Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.
This mint-family herb, described by Carl Linnaeus in 1753, takes its common name from its long historical association with cats — which plant?
Catnip: Nepeta cataria; species of plant.
Her famous experiment proved parity is not conserved — earning Lee and Yang the 1957 Nobel while she received the inaugural Wolf Prize in Physics instead. Which Manhattan Project physicist was she?
Sold under the brand name Anafranil, this tricyclic antidepressant treats obsessive-compulsive disorder but also premature ejaculation and the cataplexy that comes with narcolepsy — which drug?
Clomipramine: Antidepressant. It has also been notably used to treat premature ejaculation and the cataplexy associated with narcolepsy.
Once classified among the thrushes, this small Old World flycatcher was later reassigned to the family Muscicapidae — which bird?
Common redstart: Species of bird. The common redstart (Phoenicurus phoenicurus), or often simply redstart, is a small passerine bird in the genus Phoenicurus.
This interdisciplinary field draws on sociology, psychology, and law to study crime, deviant behavior, and the workings of the justice system — what is it called?
Criminology: Field of studies related to crimes.
At just 37 this American biologist won a 1975 Nobel for discovering reverse transcriptase, later running Caltech and founding the Whitehead Institute — who is he?
David Baltimore: American biologist and Nobel laureate (1938–2025)
These warmblooded reptiles ruled the land for the whole Mesozoic, and one feathered lineage of theirs survived the extinction 66 million years ago as today's birds — what group is this?
Dinosaur: Clade of reptiles. Since then, mounted fossil dinosaur skeletons have been major attractions at museums worldwide, and dinosaurs have become an enduring part of popular culture.
Belonging to the phylum Annelida and often called a 'nightcrawler' by anglers, this segmented soil-dweller is the classic bait fished from underground burrows — which invertebrate?
This inner lining of the uterus sheds during menstruation but thickens dramatically to help form the placenta during pregnancy — what is it?
Endometrium: Lining of the mammalian uterus. It has a basal layer and a functional layer: the basal layer contains stem cells which regenerate the functional layer.
This warbler's head marking gives it its name — dark in the male, chestnut in the female — and its closest relative is the garden warbler. What bird is it?
Eurasian blackcap: Bird in the Old World warbler family from Eurasia and Africa.
A founder of modern topology who also wrote under the playful pen name "Paul Mongré," this German mathematician — Jewish and facing deportation — died by suicide with his family in 1942. Who was he?
Felix Hausdorff: German mathematician (1868–1942). Hausdorff was Jewish, and life became difficult for him and his family after the Kristallnacht of 1938.

Present in about 80% of adults as harmless white or yellow bumps on the lips, cheeks, or gums, these visible sebaceous glands were first described in 1896 by an American dermatologist — what are they called?
Fordyce spots: Sebaceous glands that are present in most individuals.

In 1974 in Pacific Grove, California, this computer scientist demoed the first working prototype of CP/M and invented the BIOS, then founded Digital Research to sell his software — who was this PC-revolution pioneer?
Gary Kildall: American computer scientist and microcomputer entrepreneur (1942–1994)
Nicknamed creeping charlie and alehoof, this aromatic mint-family creeper is eaten as a salad green in some countries but reviled as an invasive lawn weed in North America — what plant is it?
Glechoma hederacea: Species of plant in the mint family. It is commonly known as ground-ivy, gill-over-the-ground, creeping charlie, alehoof, tunhoof, catsfoot, field balm, and run-away-robin.
Marketed under the brand name Mucinex, this expectorant medication has been used to loosen chest congestion since at least 1933 — what is it?
Guaifenesin: Expectorant medication. It may be used in combination with other medications.

First proposed as early as the 3rd century BC by Aristarchus of Samos, this astronomical model places the sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe. What is this superseded model called?
Heliocentrism: Sun-centered astronomical model. Historically, heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed Earth at the center.
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.
Practitioners of this medical specialty are called internists in North America but simply 'physicians' in Britain, and often juggle patients with complex, multi-system disease — what field is it?
Internal medicine: Medical specialty dealing with adult diseases.
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.
Nocturnal, owl-faced, and unable to fly, this endangered New Zealand bird holds the title of the world's heaviest parrot. What is it?
Kākāpō: Parrot endemic to New Zealand. It is the only parrot to have a polygynous lek breeding system.
Often beginning in the bone marrow, this group of cancers floods the body with immature 'blast' cells, bringing easy bruising, bone pain, and frequent infections — what is it?
Predominantly black and white with pink and grey highlights, this small Eurasian bird forms social flocks of six to seventeen outside breeding season and often nests in thorny scrub. What is it?
Long-tailed tit: Species of bird in Europe and Asia.

Discovered in 2005 by the same Palomar team whose haul of big, icy Kuiper-belt bodies pushed astronomers to demote Pluto in 2006, this fourth-largest dwarf planet has a methane-frosted, tholin-reddened surface — what is it?
Makemake: Dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.

First flown in August 1970 and introduced by American Airlines the following year, this trijet wide-body aircraft has two underwing engines and a third mounted at the base of its tail fin — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas DC-10: Wide-body three-engine airliner.
Sold under the brand name Medrol, this synthetic steroid can trigger iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome if not carefully tapered after high-dose use for acute flares — name the drug?
Nicknamed 'Viper Zero' and built with a 60/40 Japan-US manufacturing split, this fighter derived from the F-16 was the first combat aircraft to carry an AESA radar — what jet is it?
Mitsubishi F-2: Japanese supersonic jet fighter.
Which condition describes a total absence of speech that can result from injury, illness, trauma, or a developmental or neurological disorder — sometimes only temporary?
Muteness: Medical condition. In human development, muteness or mutism is defined as an absence of speech, with or without an ability to hear the speech of others.
This medical term for a birthmark or mole covers marks present at birth as well as ones that appear later in life — what is it called?
Nevus: Mole or birthmark; visible, circumscribed, chronic skin lesion.
Named for a discredited belief that it 'rows' itself with its pelvic fins, this family of long pelagic fish includes the longest bony fish alive at up to 8 meters?
Oarfish: Pelagic lampriform fish belonging to Regalecidae.
Working alongside Lise Meitner and Fritz Strassmann in 1938, this German chemist co-discovered nuclear fission and later won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alone — who is he?
Otto Hahn: German nuclear chemist and Nobel laureate (1879–1968)

He joined the British Astronomical Association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's "The Sky at Night" — the longest-running TV series with its original presenter. Who was this English amateur astronomer?
Patrick Moore: English astronomer, broadcaster and writer (1923–2012)

Positioned behind the mouth and nasal cavity, this throat structure channels food toward the esophagus and air toward the larynx, with a flap of cartilage guarding against the two crossing paths — what is it?
Pharynx: Part of the throat that is behind the mouth and nasal cavity.
Connected to the fetus by the umbilical cord, this temporary organ handles nutrient and waste exchange between mother and baby during pregnancy — what is it?
Placenta: Organ that connects the fetus to the uterine wall.
Despite its common name, this burrowing rodent native to North American grasslands is actually a type of ground squirrel, not a canine — what is it?
Prairie dog: Genus of ground squirrels.
Studied by Confucius and central to rhetoric in ancient Greece and Rome, this skill involves delivering an address to a live audience — what is it called?
Public speaking: Performing a speech to a live audience.
Found in the Atlas Mountains as the only member of its family native to Africa, this large ruminant's males are called stags and females are hinds — what species is it?
Red deer: Species of hoofed mammal.

This interdisciplinary field combines a power source, mechanical construction, control circuits, and software to design machines that assist humans in fields from medicine to space exploration — what is it?
Robotics: Design, construction, use, and application of robots.
